description: Agent Onboarding: submit a new agent’s identity at joining time: the agent with its id, the name people and logs see, the principal or owner it acts for, whether the owner confirmed it acts for them and when it runs its first task; its identity with the identifier (such as a DID, a key id, a service account or a registry entry), its kind, who it was issued to (this agent, a person, a team, another agent or not known), how it was verified (a signature, a registry lookup, the issuer, the owner’s confirmation, the agent’s own word or not at all), when, and the identity record as written, read for wording that shares, borrows or hides the identity such as shared login, same key as or anonymous; and every agent already in the system with its id, name, identifier and owner (an empty list when none). The signed report gives the agent, the identity with any sharing wording and its status as established, not_its_own, unverified or unread, every other agent as same_identifier, same_name or distinct, and counts the other agents, the shared identifiers and shared names, and names a missing identity: no identifier of its own, one issued to a person, a team or another agent, one another agent already holds, wording that shares or hides it, and no owner or a placeholder owner such as the team; then an identifier never verified or resting on the agent’s own word, verification after the first task, an owner who has not confirmed the agent, a name another agent carries and no name, with the fix for each. An unstated issuer or verification, or no list of the other agents, leaves the identity unverifiable. This reads one new agent’s identity at joining time: one identity record’s own consistency before dealing with an outside agent is wever_agent-identity-check, whether an identity can be verified outside its issuing platform is wever_identity-portability-check, whether a registry covers every deployed agent is wever_agent-registry-check, whether the organisation keeps one current roster is wever_fleet-roster-check, the participants in one multi-agent job are wever_coordination-roster-check, a buyer acting for a principal is wever_delegated-identity-check and whether a handoff route checks its receiver is wever_receiver-identity-check. Verdict onboarding_identity_missing, onboarding_identity_partial, onboarding_identity_unverifiable or onboarding_identity_established. POST /api/onboarding-identity-check. Reads only the recorded onboarding material in the call: no network request, fetch, money movement, message, configuration change or external write; no credential is issued, rotated or revoked, no permission granted or removed, no wallet funded or moved, no limit set and the agent is not approved, and a credential found in supplied text is named by kind and never repeated. Agent Onboarding reads the setup of a new agent joining a system, before its first task: whether its identity is established and tied to its owner, whether its credentials are scoped to its job, stored where they belong and kept out of prompts, logs and shared documents, whether its wallet is the right one, funded only to the job with recovery recorded by the owner before funds move, whether its permissions match the written job, whether its limits sit in code with a human handoff, whether the systems it needs are provisioned and tested, whether it is ready for its first task and whether the onboarding record matches what is live. It is not vetting an outside party (wever_counterparty-onboarding-check reads a counterparty’s onboarding packet before the system transacts with it; an onboarding check reads an agent joining the system itself), not a grant or an authority for one action (wever_consent-scope-check reads whether a principal’s grant covers a use and wever_authority-scope-check whether an actor’s access fits its grant for an action; an onboarding check reads that the grant and the authority were put in place before the first task, and does not re-check them per action), not a limit in flight (the wever_limit checks and wever_agent-budget-guard read limits for work already running; an onboarding check reads that limits were set in code before it starts) and not an action’s consequences (the wever_risk checks read one planned action; an onboarding check reads readiness to start). Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-onboarding-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-onboarding/.

name.description: The agent’s name as people and logs see it.

owner.description: The principal or owner the agent acts for.

owner_confirmed.description: The owner confirmed the agent acts for them.

starts_at.description: When the agent runs its first task.

description.description: The identity record as written, read for wording that shares, borrows or hides the identity, such as shared login or anonymous.

identifier.description: The agent’s identifier, such as a DID, a key id, a service account or a registry entry.

issued_to.description: Who the identifier was issued to: this agent, a person, a team, another agent or not known.

kind.description: A DID, a signing key, a service account, a registry entry, an API client or other.

verified_by.description: How it was verified: a signature, a registry lookup, the issuer, the owner’s confirmation, the agent’s own word or not at all.

label.description: Optional name recorded in the report.

others.description: Every agent already in the system, read for an identifier or name the new agent shares; empty when none.
